summary: Extend cherry steps to bases with confluent double roots, preserving lattice splitting and window limits beyond the tested arcs.
Seek an interlacing or index rule for real Hm zeros to locate exceptional window values and organize their repair by extra rows.
Test applicable multiple-orthogonal asymptotics for large-index Hm nonvanishing away from limiting zero curves, leaving finite exact checks.
Realize window kernels in a fixed-degree bundle family and use generic balanced splitting to derive uniform Forney indices.
Construct a recursive full-rank basis pattern surviving every modulus specialization, beyond generic uniformity of the window matroid.
Prove quotient-minor ideals have no common zeros off c(c−1)=0, distinguishing zero coprimeness from a trivial factor gcd.
Use the proved exponential limit and top forms to seek a deformation to λ=3/2 without new isolated rank-drop zeros.
Prove independence of the two determinantal conditions at candidate roots to exclude common zeros of window minors and X(d,c).
Seek a shift-index recurrence separating pure-determinant candidate roots, accounting for their constant degree rather than assuming orthogonality.
Compare residual decay with height-based Mahler separation bounds as margin calibration; these bounds assume, rather than prove, coprimality.
Seek uniform modular gcd certificates with no degree drop, combining structured matrices and Lucas reduction beyond fixed-m coprimality checks.
Construct actual limit-linear-series aspects for pair functions so node additivity proves cherry, tie and triple steps uniformly.
Determine whether leading tie-cluster sums are single Schur values, then control root-of-unity exceptions to window nonvanishing.
Test root-of-unity degenerations of leading Schur sums and find alternative surviving window terms at exceptional tie moduli.
Use genuine Schur-value formulas to locate possible tie-modulus zeros on the unit circle; do not extend this to failed pure-determinant analogies.
Derive tau-function recurrences proving consecutive pure determinants coprime and test bordered extensions carrying the non-pure rows.
Use one-singularity Hermite–Padé normality as a base for adding singular points; existing perfectness hypotheses do not cover the two-point case.
Test a sector-sensitive non-crossing mechanism for full window rank, separating single-minor zeros from simultaneous cross-sector vanishing.
Prove multi-row caterpillar penalties scale by scale as nonnegative integer linear forms, additive over surplus rows.
Use valuated-matroid exchange to prove discrete convexity of class minima indexed by negative-column count for every tree.
Prove non-window terms are dominated by same or adjacent filling windows, reducing graded coefficient comparisons to neighbouring windows.
Test window domination through the Pareto front of valuation costs, checking whether adding non-window terms changes the front.
Verify M-convex aggregation by negative-column count to prove class-minimum convexity and adjacent leading windows.
Seek additional demand-structure conditions forcing interval leaders in the gross-substitutes interpretation of Plücker valuations.
Prove local single-exchange optimality of leading windows using true arc valuations, including cancellation rather than only termwise costs.
Find positive or subtraction-free exchange-minor expansions on real configurations, while retaining complex-arc cancellation limitations.
Check whether the node weight bound needs intervals or only support dimension, to extend cherry steps to arbitrary (2M+1)-element support unions.
Use positive B-spline moment representations to prove exchange inequalities on real noncancelling arcs, without claiming the complex case.
Describe complex Hankel cancellation through isotropic Gram forms and exploit real definiteness for real-arc noncancellation proofs.
Distinguish genuine q-adic valuations from modular isotropic cancellation by verifying Hankel units or explicitly accounting for their powers.
Derive ternary face-minor unit conditions from carry counts in hook-type plane-partition factors.
Prove uniform joint-operator root support, window rank and singular-part independence to exclude nonzero triple-row combinations vanishing on windows.
Use real-modulus recurrence oscillation to constrain triple-row window zeros, recording which singularity controls each row's sign pattern.
Construct an explicit two-vector dual of the triple window so complementary minors reduce rank loss to a smaller proportionality condition.
Derive all-m hypergeometric formulas for triple-window entries via Appell and fractional integrals, checking whether transformed tails truncate.
Expand top-shift coefficients in Schur–Hankel terms, retaining the Hankel-free contribution required by equilateral controls.
Extend elimination to two raised columns and verify the predicted (1,1) Schur–Hankel term exactly at M=3,4.
Derive infinity exponents and Frobenius recursion for the joint operator to prove the triple criterion's vanishing triangle and root block.
Combine root-of-unity power sums with a proved multi-column expansion to identify rectangular Schur–Hankel leaders at regular polygons.
Use momentum-selection identities for polygon subset sums and develop controlled perturbations for clusters near regular polygons.
Analyze polygon residuals and nearby clusters through bilinear harmonic-frame Gram matrices, distinguishing them from Hermitian Grams.
Express next graded window coefficients through neighbouring least coefficients to prove flow-order vanishing, checking all surviving neighbours.
Expand flow derivatives of Hankel sums by Schur rules to identify surviving weight-two leaders at exact flow order two.
Test lowest-surviving-excitation leadership while allowing either single or double raises; the naive doubles-only prediction already failed.
Extend the top-up scaling identity to all graded coefficients to force family vanishing below the cluster's flow order.
